sources.title: The Viṣṇu Purāṇa, Book 4, chapter 18: Yayāti’s son Anu and the Anga line
sources.edition: McComas Taylor, trans., The Viṣṇu Purāṇa: Ancient Annals of the God with Lotus Eyes (ANU Press, 2021), Book 4, chapter 18; locators follow the chapter/verse numbering used by the ANU translation and its selective index.
sources.cross_check: Sanskrit and IAST checked selectively against https://eternalraga.com/en/scriptures/puranas/vishnu-purana/4/18 (Aṃśa 4, chapter 18; its web segmentation does not map one-to-one to ANU verse numbers). This transcription differs in readings from Taylor at several names (including Sabhānala/Sabhānara, the Uśīnara sons, Ruśadratha/Ruṣadratha, Suhma/Suhya, and Atiratha/Adhiratha); claims follow Taylor’s ANU translation and are not harmonized.

notes: Chapter scope is 4.18 only. Existing vp_yayati and vp_anu nodes are referenced as anchors, not redefined here. A separate Yayāti→Anu claim preserves chapter 18 as an additional witness to the relationship already recorded from chapter 10.

The ANU rendering supplies named persons through Vṛṣasena. Its selective index gives specific locators including Mahāmanas and Titikṣu (4.18.1), Daśaratha son of Aja and son of Romapāda (4.18.2), and Adhiratha son of Satyakarman (4.18.5). The 4.18.1 Yayāti→Anu edge is retained as a distinct chapter-18 witness alongside the existing chapter-10 claim.

Potential namesakes are separate: Anu-branch Janamejaya is not the Puru-line Janamejaya; Romapāda’s childless son Daśaratha is not Aja’s son Daśaratha; Bali is scoped as Titikṣu’s descendant; the five eponymous sons are not merged with their territories/peoples.
Citraratha and Romapāda are one individual because the source explicitly says he is also known by that name.
The unnamed wife of Bali is not made a node. Claims say Dīrghatamas fathered the five named sons with Bali’s wife and explicitly avoid treating Bali as their father.

Count: 56 new person nodes plus the 2 existing anchor persons (Yayāti, Anu) = 58 distinct named individuals referenced in this batch. The five Bāleya sons are individuals in the genealogy; their eponymous territories are not included as persons.
